statements.t: This management’s discussion and analysis includes statements regarding our expectations with respect to our future performance, expected business conditions, liquidity, and capital resources.

In addition to continued increases in freight costs, as a result of higher diesel fuel prices, we saw significant increases in recycled fiber, purchased power, and chemical costs during the third quarter, which we expect to continue at elevated levels.
Looking ahead as we move from the third quarter into the fourth quarter, we expect solid corrugated products demand with some seasonal improvement.

Prices for containerboard and corrugated products are expected to improve as we continue to implement earlier price increases, but corrugated products mix will be seasonally weaker with higher e-commerce volumes, partially offsetting the benefit from higher prices.

Containerboard production will be lower with maintenance outages at three of our mills, and mill maintenance outage expenses, including the impact on production volume from those fourth quarter outages, will be significantly higher in the fourth quarter.
We expect seasonally lower volume and slightly higher prices in the Paper segment.
We expect freight costs to increase across our business with diesel fuel prices increasing above third quarter levels.
We also expect costs for recycled fiber to continue to increase as well as higher wood fiber costs due to winter yields and mill mix.
Considering these items, we expect fourth quarter earnings to be lower than the third quarter of 2026, excluding special items.

We believe that net cash generated from operating activities, cash on hand, available borrowings under our revolving credit facility, and available capital through access to capital markets will be adequate to meet our liquidity and capital requirements, including payments of any declared common stock dividends, for the foreseeable future.
As our debt or credit facilities become due, we will need to repay, extend, or replace such facilities.
Our ability to do so will be subject to future economic conditions and financial, business, and other factors, many of which are beyond our control.
We expect capital investments in 2026 to be within a range of $865 million to $890 million.
We currently estimate capital expenditures to comply with environmental regulations will be about $21 million in 2026.
The write-off of expenditures related to sustainability and renewable energy projects was recorded following the Company’s decision to defer a specific carbon capture initiative at this time.

statements.t: Our mills ran at full capacity during the quarter, and we are meaningfully realizing production benefits from projects at our Jackson mill as well as improved operating performance at the acquired Greif mills.

Our white paper operations turned in another excellent quarter, with higher than expected sales volumes, strong price realization and safe and successful completion of the maintenance outage at the International Falls mill.”
Kowlzan added, “Looking ahead as we move from the third quarter into the fourth quarter, we expect solid corrugated products demand with some seasonal improvement.

Prices for containerboard and corrugated products are expected to improve as we continue to implement earlier price increases, but corrugated products mix will be seasonally weaker with higher e-commerce volumes.

Containerboard production will be lower with maintenance outages at three of our mills, and mill maintenance outage expenses, including the impact on production volume from fourth quarter outages, will be significantly higher in the fourth quarter.
We expect seasonally lower volume and slightly higher prices in the Paper segment.
We expect freight costs to increase with diesel fuel prices increasing above third quarter levels.
We also expect costs for recycled fiber to continue to increase as well as higher wood fiber costs due to winter yields and mill mix.
Considering these items, we expect fourth quarter earnings of $2.81 per share, excluding special items.”

We currently expect to incur acquisition and integration related costs and costs related to the closure of corrugated products facilities during the fourth quarter; however, additional special items may arise due to fourth quarter events.
